the relationship between social support and mental health in disasters is complex, and the relationship between social status and mental health may be indirect and mediated through social support.

in the context of disaster, the effect of social support on depression is more significant than socioeconomic status, but that social support may be more important in the context of some disasters than in the context of others.

the effects of disasters on mental health are not uniform, but are mediated by local conditions, and that the role of social support is critical to the understanding of mental health vulnerability in the aftermath of disasters.

social support is an important protective factor for mental health in disasters.
